title: One Thing You Must Ask Yourself Before Next School Year
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Drawing from his personal coaching practice, Linsin shares a self-inventory exercise that has helped many teachers pinpoint the single weakness driving most of their classroom management struggles. Teachers identify their 'one thing' — the area where they were weakest the previous year — and then list its downstream negative consequences, such as lost respect or rising stress. He argues that although several weak areas may exist, one usually stands out as the underlying catalyst for the rest, and once identified, it's often the only thing that needs fixing. Common examples include inconsistency, moving or talking too fast, micromanagement, and unclear rules, and naming the root cause typically brings both clarity and relief.
points: Presents a self-inventory exercise built on a single diagnostic question: what was your weakest area of classroom management last year?
Instructs teachers to bullet-point the specific negative consequences that flow from that one weakness.
Argues that one root weakness is often the catalyst that causes or worsens several other struggles.
Lists common 'one things' including inconsistency, moving/talking too fast, micromanagement, and unclear rules.
Reports that naming the root weakness gives coaching clients clarity and relief, showing they are closer to success than they believed.
quotes: If you had to pinpoint one area of classroom management in which you were weakest this past school year, what would it be?
In other words, what is your one thing , your Achilles’ heel that is mucking up all the rest?
Your one thing is undermining and making harder all your other strategies and efforts to control your classroom and enjoy teaching.
Once I started using this process with my coaching clients, we were able to zero in on the ‘why’ of their struggles almost immediately.
They also learned to their relief that they weren’t as far away from having a well-behaved class as they once thought.
Inconsistency. Moving and talking too fast. Micromanagement. Taking misbehavior personally.
